subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a diminutive form of Daz'issin, a name mothers in Menzoberranzan used for sons they wished to protect, with fewer than a handful of recorded uses in the last three centuries, and associated houses that have all perished.
source_quote: She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a keeper of restricted knowledge in Menzoberranzan, maintaining a pose of neutral informant while her body language — five minutes of practiced stillness contradicting her words — reveals she is carefully navigating what she can say, knowing more than the public record allows.
source_quote: She had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Houses that used Daz'issin
fact: The noble houses that historically used the name Daz'issin have all perished, with no known survivors or continuations in the last three centuries, suggesting systematic eradication or collapse.
source_quote: The houses that had those names have all gone.

subject: Heraldry book: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text, partially defaced by a deliberate, razor-cut removal of an appendix referenced by a footnote on Daz'issin, indicating intentional suppression of information tied to the name and its lineage.
source_quote: A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Two distinct groups of mercenaries are actively tracking Daz — one to ensure his survival, the other to kill him — suggesting his identity or lineage is of high strategic value and contested between opposing powers.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: Missing appendix on Daz'issin
fact: The appendix referenced in the footnote on Daz'issin has been physically excised from the heraldry book, creating an unresolved gap in the historical record that may contain the truth of Daz's origins, the fate of his house, or the identity of his protector.

subject: Silence of Yvenne
fact: Yvenne’s refusal to answer the question 'What if they weren't successfully all gone?' constitutes a deliberate, non-verbal affirmation in Menzoberranzan’s culture — where silence in the ledger is an answer — implying that at least one house or lineage tied to Daz'issin may still endure.
source_quote: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where reading rooms, interpreting body language, and recognizing when someone’s posture contradicts their speech are essential survival skills — and where silence, omission, and defaced texts are tools of power and concealment.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.
